name: Longto
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich (avec l'assistance de Illiassou Godje et Bouba Bakary). 2012 [digital edn 2021, 'Dictionnaire lɔŋto ACAD 1.0']. Lexique Lɔ̀ŋtó (~ Voko) - Français. Poli: Lamido de Voko / Comité de Développement du Lamidat de Voko / DFG. 68 pp.
tone_statements.quote: La langue lɔŋto a trois hauteurs tonales : haut, moyen et bas. Il y a aussi deux tons descendants : haut-bas et rarement moyen-bas. En général les sons qui portent les tons sont les voyelles, et parfois /l/ ~ /r/ et les nasales /m/ ~ /n/ et /ŋ/ s'ils sont les seuls sons d'un morphème ou en position finale d'un mot ou morphème. [...] En général les tons descendants sont exclusivement prononcés à la fin d'une phrase.
tone_statements.translation: The Lɔŋto language has three tone heights: high, mid and low. There are also two falling tones: high-low and, rarely, mid-low. In general the sounds that bear the tones are the vowels, and sometimes /l/ ~ /r/ and the nasals /m/ ~ /n/ and /ŋ/ if they are the only sounds of a morpheme or stand in final position of a word or morpheme. [...] In general the falling tones are pronounced exclusively at the end of a sentence.
tone_statements.locator: p. 4, section 1.2 'Le ton'; infinitive tone restriction in 2.1 on the same page
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + 2 falling (HL, rare ML)

sources.note: Grammatical introduction pp. 3-9 has 1.1 L'alphabet (p. 3) and 1.2 Le ton (p. 4): three tone heights H/M/L plus falling HL and (rarely) ML; TBUs vowels, sometimes l/r and nasals; falling tones only phrase-finally; infinitive tone restriction (2.1). Nothing on stress/accent/prominence ('accent' occurs only as the names of the tone diacritics).

En général les sons qui portent les tons sont les voyelles, et parfois /l/ ~ /r/ et les nasales /m/ ~ /n/ et /ŋ/ s'ils sont les seuls sons d'un morphème ou en position finale d'un mot ou morphème. tone.translation: The Lɔŋto language has three tone heights: high, mid and low. There are also two falling tones: high-low and, rarely, mid-low. In general the sounds that bear the tones are the vowels, and sometimes /l/ ~ /r/ and the nasals /m/ ~ /n/ and /ŋ/ if they are the only sounds of a morpheme or stand in final position of a word or morpheme. tone.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + 2 falling (HL, rare ML)
tone.says: Three tone heights (high, mid, low) plus two falling tones (high-low; mid-low rare); tone-bearing units are vowels and, when morpheme-final or the only segment of a morpheme, /l~r/ and nasals /m n ŋ/; H marked with acute, L with grave, M with macron or left unmarked, HL circumflex; falling tones are pronounced only phrase-finally; section 2.1 adds that no infinitive begins with a low tone on its first syllable. Nothing on stress/accent.
